steps.text: TWENTY YEARS EARLIER // SECTOR 9. Fresh Dominion steel has been bolted over an older chamber that refuses to stay quiet.

steps.speaker: Lab PA
steps.text: SOURCE BEAST CONTAINMENT BREACH. ALL PERSONNEL CLEAR THE STASIS FLOOR.
The far doors bow inward. Orion tears a brass Chime from the signal cradle while something enormous leans against the other side.

steps.speaker: Orion
steps.text: Chorus, carry this beyond the seal. Let it be louder than I am.
He fires the Chime through an emergency launch tube. Its identity signal streaks away from the facility, calling for help and drawing the hunt with it.

steps.speaker: Orion
steps.text: Mute my signal. Now.
The stasis glass seals. The chamber goes silent. Outside, the Chime keeps running through the dark.
A low harmonic resonance vibrates through the metal floor plates, rising from the deep oceanic current below.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: Do you feel that? The pressure... it's changing.
The air grows heavy, carrying the distant echo of a song long forgotten.
The squad retreats to regroup after the defeat.
Patch up, recharge shields, and consider buffing allies before re-engaging. Status items and defensive skills can swing the next encounter.
A security lock halts your progress.
Check your objectives or inventory—certain rooms need power restored or a keycard before they open.
Sensors flag movement beyond the doorway.
Clear nearby threats or prepare a pre-emptive strike—some exits stay sealed until the ambush is dealt with.

steps.speaker: Ollie
steps.text: Nova! There you are! We're late to meet Jed.

steps.speaker: Ollie
steps.text: Touch my name on your HUD, choose Talk, and let's catch up to him before he locks up.
The generator hums to life, flooding the tunnels with light.
Somewhere deeper within the mine, heavy locks release.
Ellie carefully packs the shattered display into a crate for repair.
Maddie hands over the grinder, hopeful you can repair it.
Kasey reluctantly passes you the cracked projector lens.
Jed celebrates as all three relics return to the workshop.
Colony camera feeds cycle through wide, close, and tracking angles for visual calibration.
The view locks, drifts, then settles as the scene framing comes online.
Status captions pulse across the feed, translating colony alarms into something readable.
The caption layer holds long enough to read before the next warning takes its place.
Narration settles over the scene like a system log with a pulse.
Emergency color grading washes the image in warning reds and cold industrial blues.
The scene fades down until only the colony hum remains.
A white impact flare swallows the frame, then snaps back to the room.
A fractured memory cuts through the present, bright at the edges and gone too fast.
The frame narrows, focusing attention on the single choice left in front of Nova.
Trade Row opens into noise, heat, and a dozen quiet deals pretending to be legal.
Every visual layer stacks together: motion, captions, filters, and the pressure of the moment.
The narrator catches the quiet detail the alarms are too loud to notice.
A shift buzzer rattles the bunk wall. Below, the first drill cage drops and the quota clock starts counting.
The camera glides across the room, letting the damage tell the story first.
Dust, sparks, and tiny motes of resonance drift through the light.
A ring of pressure ripples outward, bending the air into visible sound.
Jed taps the bench twice, already watching to see whether Nova remembers the first rule: power off before hands in.
The cutter settles into a steady hum. Jed tries not to look proud and fails by half an inch.
Nova feathers the trigger. The cutter climbs past its factory limit, the repaired cold loop whining as every work light turns white.

steps.speaker: Jed
steps.text: Kill it!

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: It is off. That hum is not mine.
A lower note answers through the workshop floor. Then a sector breaker blows, and the Dominion terminal quietly attaches Nova's ID to the fault.
The shattered display slides onto Jed's bench, another broken thing waiting for stubborn hands.
The grinder lands with a heavy clunk, smelling of dust, old grease, and useful trouble.
The cracked projector lens catches the work light, splitting it into tired little rainbows.
The frame jolts as something heavy hits nearby.
Motion streaks tear past the viewport as the launch rail takes hold.
The horizon tips sideways, making the corridor feel even less trustworthy.
The open square catches every sound at once: boots, vendors, distant machinery, and the low electric buzz of surveillance.
The visual effects layer blooms across the frame, then folds back into the scene.
The edges darken, pulling the eye toward the one detail that matters.
A hard transition sweeps the old room away and leaves the next danger waiting.
The view tightens slowly, closing the distance before anyone moves.
The camera pushes forward and tracks sideways, following the line of trouble through the room.

steps.speaker: Ollie
steps.text: Nova! There you are! We're late to meet Jed.

steps.speaker: Ollie
steps.text: Touch my name on your HUD, choose Talk, and let's catch up to him before he locks up.
The cutter reaches eighty-seven kilohertz. The Tuning Fork answers, and two frequencies settle into one clean pressure wave.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: Same pulse as the workshop. My surge woke you.
The damaged cradle closes the circuit through the cutter. Jed's Cryo-Inductor holds the heat. The Flux Liner throws a blue arc into the floor instead of Nova's heart.

steps.speaker: Unknown System
steps.text: CALIBRATION SIGNAL ACCEPTED. OPERATOR HANDSHAKE INCOMPLETE. COMPLETING THROUGH AVAILABLE CIRCUIT.

The chamber skips. Nova is suddenly on one knee, her suit clock missing half a second she never perceived. The cold-loop coil has fused, the liner's ground strip is black, and a new protocol is ringing through her nerves.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: Not a prophecy. A machine handshake—and it just logged me in.
The pod clears the magnetic launch rail, shooting up into the upper atmosphere. The glowing canyons of the colony shrink into a tiny gray scar below.
Suddenly, the view out the viewport fractures. A blinding web of blue resonance—the planetary shield—flashes in front of you.
The pod's hull begins to shriek and buckle as it collides with the shield's standing wave frequency.

steps.speaker: Zeke
steps.text: Nova! Hold on! Authorization passed and the beacon route locked, but there is no Shield corridor in this flight plan!
Alarms scream. The navigation console sparks and dies. Zeke holds onto the frame, yelling over the sound of tearing metal.
The shield rejects the pod, throwing it back into the atmosphere in a spinning descent toward the overgrown ruins of Sector 9.
Everything goes white as the thrusters fail and the ground rushes up to meet you.
Night settles over Canopy Ridge. Nova reaches the Bridge's Link toward Zeke's reopened cut; static whites out her sight, and her knees strike stone.

steps.speaker: Orion
steps.text: Stop. You are burning the wire.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: I can hold it.

steps.speaker: Orion
steps.text: The Bridge connects; it does not make one body carry the circuit. Ground first. Then channel.
Zeke clips a grounding lead to Nova's bracer. Gh0st offers his armored hand without an order forcing it. Orion holds one low tuning tone until all four breaths fall into time.

steps.speaker: Gh0st
steps.text: No command attached. I am here. Route it.
Nova opens Link. Current passes among them without merging them; Zeke's wound stabilizes while every thought remains its owner's.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: Link. Not merge. I get it.
You plug your datapad into the console's debugging interface. The screen immediately cascades with thousands of lines of encrypted compiler scripts.
A hidden data block decrypts. The signature on the package is marked by standing waves and acoustic patterns, signed by the 'Chorus'.
The terminal chimes. 'Protocol override successfully broadcast. Local admin privileges established.'
You boot up the discarded datapad. The battery is critically low, but the final text log is intact.
Log Entry: 'They sealed the doors from the outside. Said the collapse was a biohazard risk, but we only hit a pocket of hum.'
Log Entry: 'The resonance is beautiful. It doesn't sound like a machine. It sounds like currents in a deep ocean. I'm not afraid of the dark anymore.'
The screen flickers and goes dark permanently, leaving you in the cold silence of the mine.
The Ascended falls, but Vale's code remains inside the collapsing Source. Six Echoes hum behind safety latches that cannot carry enough signal.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: I am not a cup. I am a wire. Form the circuit.
Zeke takes her right hand and grounds the current. Gh0st braces her back as his armor vents white heat. Orion grips her shoulder and tunes the chaos into one answer.

steps.speaker: Orion
steps.text: No. We are Starborn.
Nova opens the Key. The Source hits them like an ocean of white light. They hold together, fire the Tuned Note, and the Tear closes.
They fall together.
Morning in the Colony. A corridor stands open through the planetary curtain. Dominion insignia come down by hand; nobody mistakes an opening for a finished revolution.

At Zeke's diner, Nova steadies a mug in her trembling tuning hand and studies a photograph of the crew at Tideglass Beach. She remembers the sand, the salt, and exactly who threw the first canteen. A thin signal whine still threads behind everything she hears.

steps.speaker: Zeke
steps.text: Set the mug down before your hand votes against you. The tremor is worse when you're tired.

steps.speaker: Gh0st
steps.text: You threw the canteen at me. Accuracy: 94%. You remember losing the argument.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: I remember the beach. The music is gone. The signal whine isn't.

steps.speaker: Orion
steps.text: It may fade. Until then, listen past it. The wind is still there.

steps.speaker: Nova
steps.text: Sounds like a good day. Tell it again?

steps.speaker: Zeke
steps.text: Pull up a chair. It is a long story.
